newsitem.title: USA: Milk prices, already lofty, to climb in 1997 - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Milk prices, already lofty, to climb in 1997 - USDA.

text.p: The farm-gate price for milk, already at lofty levels, will climb even higher in 1997, the U.S. Agriculture Department forecast Wednesday.

USDA estimated an all-milk price of $14.55-$15.35 per cwt in 1997, compared to its forecast of $14.35-$14.45 for this year. Its forecast for 1997 was a sharp increase from the $12.70-$13.60 average that was forecast a month ago.
Prices would be buoyed, USDA indicated, by milk output that would rise only one billion lbs, to 161.1 billion, instead of the 1.9 billion increase expected earlier for 1997.
USDA boosted its forecast of beef production this year.
Beef output was pegged at 25.851 billion lbs this year, up 121 million lbs from the August forecast. USDA maintained its estimate of 1997 beef production of 26.057 billion lbs.
Pork output was again forecast at 17.105 billion lbs this year and 17.388 billion lbs in 1997.
Broiler production was forecast to climb to 26.207 billion lbs this year, up 13 million from last month's forecast. Output for 1997 was pegged at 26.673 billion lbs, same as in August.
Overall, USDA forecast meat consumption at 210.2 lbs per person this year and 212.2 lbs per capita in 1997.
